title: Conditions on a boiling point
body: Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure of 101.325 kilopascals. Lower external pressure lowers its boiling point. Boiling occurs when the liquid's vapor pressure equals the external pressure. The value 100 degrees Celsius is not a universal boiling point at every altitude or pressure.

reference.question: What must the vapor pressure equal for a liquid to boil?
